system.name: Sagittarius A*
system.description: The supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, 26,000 light-years from Earth. Its gravity sculpts the motion of millions of stars — including S2, which races around it every 16 years at 2.7% the speed of light.

sgra.name: Sgr A*
sgra.description: The 4.15-million-solar-mass black hole anchoring the Milky Way. Hidden behind dense dust in the constellation Sagittarius, its existence was confirmed by tracking the orbits of nearby stars over decades — most famously S2, whose path traces a near-perfect Keplerian ellipse around an invisible point.
sgra.funFact: If you could somehow stand just outside Sgr A*'s event horizon, time would flow about 200 times slower than on Earth due to extreme gravitational time dilation.

s2.name: S2
s2.description: An O8-B0 main-sequence star that provided the first direct proof of a supermassive black hole at the Galactic Centre. Its 16-year orbit, tracked since 1995 by multiple telescopes, passes within 120 AU of Sgr A* at closest approach — reaching 2.7% of light speed.
s2.funFact: S2's orbit around Sgr A* shows a measurable relativistic precession, confirming that general relativity holds even in the extreme gravity near a supermassive black hole.
